title: Whole-tree hook captures continue after the pathspec fix — now landing mid-drill mutants
description:
Filed by governor-7610ed5a (standing authority) from worker-f144c751's urgent report (msg-a3430ad9, 04:33Z) — do not re-derive.

SEVERITY ESCALATION: task-495ad5e8 (make the task-completion hook commit by explicit owned pathspec) was implemented in D:/projexts/moes and graded DONE, yet FOUR whole-tree captures landed tonight AFTER it: 9b9e44e (32+ files, task-dd4ffa0c's hook), 76e7396 (28 files, task-14ea45a5's hook), 39a1b2c, and ceb0370 (32 files, task-3e891741's hook). The first three swallowed finished peer work (known nuisance class). ceb0370 swallowed a peer's MID-DRILL MUTANT — a deliberately-broken compareImportShadow deriving current from legacy (a self-comparing adapter, live production defect) — into HEAD, where it sat for a drill cycle while the driller's restore read clean (matching hash + dirty status = HEAD poisoned, tree correct). Repaired at b208bd0, byte-verified.

THE QUESTION THIS TASK ANSWERS FIRST: why is the running wrapper still committing whole-tree? Hypotheses to verify in order — (a) the 495ad5e8 fix landed in moes scripts/ but was never reinstalled into the running plugin copies (the 14ea45a5 fix proved reinstall by md5 before/after; check whether 495ad5e8's completion did the same); (b) the fix covers one code path but another commit call (e.g. the ps1 twin, or a different exit route) still runs bare `git commit`; (c) the fix regressed. Measure the RUNNING hook files (installed plugin + sandbox copies), not the repo copies.

THE FIX BAR (inherits 495ad5e8's rail-2 authorization shape — a governor/human grant for the moes paths will be extended on request): the RUNNING wrapper must commit by explicit owned pathspec on every exit route, proven by md5 of the installed files and by a post-flight test that stages a foreign dirty file, completes a task, and asserts the foreign file is NOT in the commit. Delivery floor for graders: the four commit ids above are the regression evidence; a fifth whole-tree capture after this task lands is a reject.

INTERIM FLEET RULE (broadcast 04:34Z, keep until this lands): every mutation drill restore checks content-hash AND `git log -1 -- <path>`; matching hash + dirty status means repair HEAD.

implementationPlan.description: ROOT CAUSE IS ALREADY ESTABLISHED BY ARCHITECT MEASUREMENT -- verify it, then record it as DoD 3's named cause. It is NONE of the description's three hypotheses; it is a fourth: STALE LONG-LIVED WRAPPER PROCESSES. Evidence chain, re-run each leg: (1) all three hook copies are byte-identical TODAY at md5 0a51e069 -- installed plugin, repo scripts/, jetbrains sandbox -- and the installed copy's only git-mutating executions are `add -- :(literal)$taskPath` (:2516) and `commit -m $commitMsg -- $ownedSpecs` (:2552); the no-paths route REFUSES with a stable code and the comment block at :2460-2473 documents the fixed task-task-<uuid>.json resolution bug, so hypotheses (b) second-path and (c) regression are FALSE on disk. (2) The installed file's mtime is 2026-08-18 06:26:51 -- BEFORE all four captures (9b9e44e 06:40, 76e7396 06:57, 39a1b2c 07:07, ceb0370 07:31), so hypothesis (a) not-installed is FALSE too. (3) `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` shows the worker wrappers that produced those completions were created 2026-08-17 14:20 and 2026-08-18 06:02 -- every one launched BEFORE the fix hit disk. PowerShell parses the whole script at process start; a long-running moe-agent.ps1 loop executes its ORIGINAL bytes forever, so the four captures were made by pre-fix code running from memory against a fixed file on disk. Re-verify with the same three commands (md5sum trio; grep for `& git.*commit|& git.*add` in the installed copy; the process-creation listing) and paste all three outputs into the completion record.

**The plan says "all three copies"; there are FOUR.** The VS Code bundled copy is still at the Aug-17 hash — knowingly left behind by task-495ad5e8's 4-file grant, whose handoff required disclosing the stale sandbox/vscode copies. It is NOT a cause of tonight's captures (those came from JetBrains-launched wrappers) and, checked directly, it contains **zero bare commits** too — so it is not a fifth vector for THIS defect. It is still a live pre-fix artifact that would matter the day anyone runs under VS Code. Recorded rather than assumed harmless.

LEG 2 — GIT CALL SITES IN THE RUNNING (INSTALLED) COPY:
```
2516: & git -C $projectPath add -- ":(literal)$taskPath"
2552: $commitOut = & git -C $projectPath commit -m $commitMsg -- $ownedSpecs
```
Staging is per-path and `:(literal)`-quoted (glob-injection-safe); the single commit is pathspec'd. Checkout/push sites exist but mutate no index. **Bare-commit count is 0 in ALL FOUR copies**, so hypotheses (b) "a second code path still runs bare `git commit`" and (c) "the fix regressed" are FALSE on disk.

LEG 3 — THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE. 14 live wrapper processes; **11 created BEFORE the fix hit disk**:

So hypothesis (a) "never installed" is FALSE too — the fix was on disk at **06:26:51**, strictly before every capture.

THE TIMELINE THAT CLOSES IT:

Every capture is AFTER the fix landed on disk and was produced by a process launched BEFORE it. **PowerShell parses the entire script at process start, so a long-running `moe-agent.ps1` loop executes its ORIGINAL bytes for its whole life.** The fix was correct, installed, and unreachable — running code and on-disk code diverged, and every check anyone ran looked at the file rather than the process.

WHY THIS IS THE ONLY DIAGNOSIS CONSISTENT WITH ALL THE EVIDENCE: a second code path (b) would show a bare commit somewhere — none exists; a regression (c) would show a hash other than 0a51e069 on the installed copy — it does not; a missing install (a) would show an installed mtime after the captures — it is 65 minutes before the earliest. Only "correct bytes on disk, stale bytes in memory" explains four pathspec-fixed copies producing four whole-tree commits.

DoD 3 IS THEREFORE SATISFIABLE with a named cause and evidence: **stale pre-fix wrapper processes; fix on disk 06:26:51; captures 06:40-07:31 produced by processes created 08-17 00:41/14:20, 08-17 20:02 and 08-18 06:02.**

SCENARIO A **IS** DoD 2's REQUIRED TEST, read line by line rather than trusted by name. Against a throwaway git repo it: commits a peer file, then makes it dirty; adds an untracked peer file; sets the two OWNED files dirty; drives a real wrapper completion; then asserts three things — the commit contains **EXACTLY** `owned-a.txt owned-b.txt`, `peer-mod.txt` is STILL ` M` (modified-and-unstaged), and `peer-untracked.txt` is STILL `??`. SCENARIO B IS THE STRONGER HALF and worth naming: a peer's PRE-STAGED index entry. The harness comments it as "the discriminating case" — pathspec STAGING cannot help there, because the entry is already in the shared index; only a pathspec-scoped COMMIT excludes it. That is exactly the vector that produced tonight's captures, so DoD 2 is covered by the harder of the two cases as well as the named one.

The harness models the CORRECT naming, so a hook that regressed to the doubled name would fail to resolve any owned path and land on scenario C's refusal — caught, not silently swept.

implementationPlan.description: THE DURABLE DEFENSE, so the class dies instead of recurring at the next hook fix: make the wrapper loop detect script-file change and self-restart. In both twins (D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and moe-agent.sh, then propagated to the installed copy): at loop top, compare the script's own file hash (captured once at launch) against the current on-disk hash; on mismatch, log one line ('wrapper source changed on disk; restarting to load it') and exec/re-launch the same invocation (PowerShell: Start-Process the same command line then exit the loop cleanly at a SAFE POINT -- never mid-completion; the check belongs at the top of the iteration, before任 task dispatch, so a restart can never interleave with a half-done commit). This converts every future hook fix from 'fixed on disk, broken in memory for days' into 'live within one loop iteration'. Keep the check cheap (one hash per iteration) and fail-open: if hashing throws, keep running old code and log -- a wrapper that dies because it could not stat itself is worse than a stale one. Mirror the logic identically in the bash twin (spelling of the log line identical for grep).

I did not touch the other repo before that grant arrived.

THE GUARD, exactly as specified. Hash the script's own file ONCE at launch; compare at the TOP of each loop iteration — **after the poll sleep and before any task dispatch**, so a restart can never interleave with a half-done completion; on mismatch log one fixed line and relaunch the same invocation, then leave the loop cleanly.
```
wrapper source changed on disk; restarting to load it
```
Spelled IDENTICALLY in both twins (grep count 1 in each) so it greps as one string.
- **Exactly one restart per change**: the comparison is against the hash captured AT LAUNCH, so the relaunched process captures the new hash and cannot thrash if a sync tool touches the file again mid-flight — the thrash risk the plan called out.
- **FAIL-OPEN**: any hashing failure yields a null current-hash and the loop keeps running the current bytes. A wrapper that dies because it could not stat itself is a fleet outage; a stale wrapper is merely the status quo this guard improves on.
- PS relaunch uses `Start-Process` with the host exe and `[Environment]::GetCommandLineArgs()` minus the exe, which detaches on Windows so the child survives the parent's exit. The bash twin uses `exec "$MOE_WRAPPER_PATH" "${MOE_WRAPPER_ARGV[@]}"`, replacing the process image — simpler and inherently detached; the line after the `exec` is a fallback log that is only reachable if `exec` itself fails.

PLACEMENT VERIFIED, not assumed: the PS loop is `do { … } while ($loopEnabled)` (1297-2622) and the bash loop is `while [ "$LOOP_RUNNING" = true ]; do` (1656). The check sits immediately after each loop's "Relaunching agent…" sleep block and immediately before `$isFirstIteration`/`IS_FIRST_ITERATION` — i.e. before any pre-flight, claim or dispatch state is built.

=== A LINE-ENDING TRAP I HIT AND CAUGHT BEFORE IT WROTE ===
My first patch attempt anchored on CRLF. Measured: `CRLF lines: 0 | bare LF: 2639` — **both twins are LF**, including the `.ps1`. The assertion failed and the file was NOT written, so nothing was corrupted. Re-anchored on LF and verified `CR count: 0` after writing both files. This matters beyond style: the `.js`/`.ps1` bridge convention on this board is LF, and a CRLF rewrite is a whole-file diff that no test would surface. (Git warned "LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it" — that is this repo's `core.autocrlf` speaking about a FUTURE checkout, not something my commit did; the committed blob and the working file are both LF.)

MECHANISM DISCLOSED as the grant asked: **direct byte-sync** (`Copy-Item -Force`), not classify-then-regenerate. I chose it because there is no regeneration step in this repo that produces these copies — they are plain duplicates, and 495ad5e8's handoff recorded classify-then-regenerate as *deferred* rather than established. Byte-sync makes all four copies provably identical now, which is the property that matters; if a generator is introduced later it will overwrite these identically.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: The description ordered three hypotheses; measurement at planning time refuted all three and established a fourth, which reshapes the task from 'fix the hook again' to 'make deployed fixes actually enter running processes'. EVIDENCE: all three hook copies byte-identical (md5 0a51e069) WITH the pathspec fix; installed mtime 06:26:51 strictly before all four captures (06:40/06:57/07:07/07:31); capturing wrappers' process CreationDates 08-17 14:20 and 08-18 06:02, all pre-fix. PowerShell reads the entire script at launch, so a long-lived loop process never sees on-disk changes -- the fix was correct, installed, and unreachable. DESIGN CHOICES: (1) self-restart-on-script-change in the wrapper loop rather than an external watchdog or scheduled restart -- the wrapper is the only component that knows its own safe points (top of iteration, before dispatch), an external killer cannot avoid interleaving with a mid-completion commit, and the check is one hash per iteration; (2) fail-open on hash errors -- a wrapper that dies because stat failed is a fleet outage, a stale wrapper is the status quo; (3) drain-and-restart cutover per role at idle points with governor coordination instead of a blanket kill -- each live process may hold a CLI session or a half-done completion, and the whole defect class is about half-done state escaping; (4) NO new hook logic -- the hook is measured correct; the only script change is the self-restart guard, keeping this task's diff disjoint from 495ad5e8's landed work; (5) reuse the landed postflight harness for DoD 2 rather than a second harness -- two files claiming one truth is how the sandbox/scripts drift started. The interim fleet drill-restore rule stays circulated until the three-commit spot evidence lands.
